title: Researched strategies
label: Historical backtests · new experiment dated 2026-11-10
method: Every result here is a NEW historical backtest run on Nov 10, 2026. None of it is forward paper, and none of it is a live signal.

Data: Yahoo Finance daily bars (split- and dividend-adjusted) for SPY, EFA, AGG, 13-week T-bill yield (^IRX) and BTC-USD, saved with SHA-256 hashes. The still-forming Nov 10 bar is dropped; the last bar used is Nov 9, 2026.

Windows: US ETFs Jan 3, 2000 to Nov 9, 2026 (dual momentum starts Oct 1, 2004 because its bond fund needs 12 months of history). Bitcoin Jan 1, 2016 to Nov 9, 2026. The recent window is a separate fresh $10,000 run from Nov 11, 2024. Published strategies with fixed settings are tested as published, but the long window is still history everyone has seen; the recent window is not a clean holdout either.
Fills: a signal from the close of day t is filled at the OPEN of day t+1 (headline numbers). Many sources assume a fill at the signal close; that version is shown as a sensitivity number.
Costs: 0.05% per side on ETFs, 0.10% per side on Bitcoin, on every traded dollar. A doubled-fee run is shown too. Idle cash in the ETF tests earns the T-bill rate; idle Bitcoin cash earns nothing.
Long only. No leverage. No shorts. No volatility sizing (so the Turtle test uses only its entry and exit channels, not its N-based position sizing).
Sharpe ratio: ETF tests use daily return above T-bills, times √252. Bitcoin tests use raw daily return, times √365. Maximum drawdown is measured on daily closes, so intraday drops could be deeper.

Verdict rule, written before the run: Promising = higher Sharpe than buy-and-hold in BOTH windows AND a shallower maximum drawdown over the long window. Failed = lower Sharpe than buy-and-hold in BOTH windows. Mixed = anything else.
10% drawdown limit: PASS only if the long-window maximum drawdown is no worse than −10%.

strategies.name: Connors RSI(2) pullback
strategies.plain: Buy the S&P 500 after a sharp two-day dip, but only while it is in a long-term uptrend; sell on the first bounce.
rules: Trend filter: close above its 200-day simple average.
Buy when the 2-day RSI (Wilder smoothing) closes below 5.
Sell when the close is above its 5-day simple average.
No stop, as the source describes. One position, all-in, long only.
strategies.interpretation: Source allows RSI below 5 or below 10; we used 5, the level the article says Connors found stronger. The short side is skipped (no shorts).

strategies.name: Faber 10-month trend filter
strategies.plain: Own the S&P 500 only while its month-end price is above its 10-month average; otherwise sit in T-bills.
rules: On the last trading day of each month, compare the month-end close with the average of the last 10 month-end closes.
Above: hold SPY. Below: hold cash earning the T-bill rate.
Ignore everything between month-ends.
strategies.interpretation: Faber tested a five-asset portfolio; this is his single-asset S&P 500 example, using SPY's adjusted price as the total-return series.

strategies.name: IBS mean reversion
strategies.plain: Buy the S&P 500 when it closes near the bottom of the day's range, sell when it closes near the top.

sources.label: QuantifiedStrategies: Internal Bar Strength rules and backtests

rules: IBS = (close − low) ÷ (high − low).
Buy when IBS is below 0.2.
Sell when IBS is above 0.8.
One position, all-in, long only.
strategies.interpretation: The source buys and sells AT the signal close. Our headline waits for the next open, which is much stricter for this strategy; the at-close number is shown as the sensitivity.

strategies.name: Turn of the month
strategies.plain: Hold the S&P 500 only for the last trading day of each month and the first three of the next.

sources.label: Quantpedia: Turn of the Month in Equity Indexes (Lakonishok & Smidt 1988)

rules: Buy so the position is held through the last trading day of the month.
Sell after the third trading day of the next month.
T-bill rate on the cash the rest of the time.
strategies.interpretation: Calendar dates are known in advance, so the source's close-to-close timing is realistic here; the headline still uses next-open fills for consistency.

strategies.name: Dual momentum (GEM)
strategies.plain: Each month, hold US stocks or foreign stocks, whichever rose more over 12 months, unless stocks are losing to T-bills, then hold bonds.

sources.label: Gary Antonacci, Optimal Momentum: Global Equities Momentum

rules: At each month-end, measure 12-month total return of SPY, EFA and T-bills.
If SPY beats T-bills, hold whichever of SPY or EFA has the higher 12-month return.
If SPY does not beat T-bills, hold AGG (US aggregate bonds).
Always fully invested in one fund.
strategies.interpretation: Antonacci uses MSCI ACWI ex-US; EFA (developed ex-US) is used because it has longer ETF history. Exact rules are in his book; this follows the published summary.

strategies.name: Golden cross 50/200
strategies.plain: Own Bitcoin while its 50-day average is above its 200-day average; cash after the death cross.
rules: Long when the 50-day simple average of closes is above the 200-day.
Cash when it is below.
Signals checked on each daily (UTC) close.
strategies.interpretation: No extra confirmation filters. Popular on crypto social media, where it is usually shown on a chart after the fact.

strategies.name: Turtle channel breakout 55/20
strategies.plain: Buy Bitcoin when it closes above its highest price of the past 55 days; sell when it closes below its 20-day low.
rules: Buy when the close is above the highest high of the prior 55 days.
Sell when the close is below the lowest low of the prior 20 days.
All-in, long only.
strategies.interpretation: Original Turtles bought intraday breakouts, sized by volatility (N), added units and used 2N stops. Volatility sizing is excluded by SIFT rules, so only the channels are tested. Related to, but different from, SIFT's 30-day breakout test.

strategies.name: MACD 12/26/9 crossover
strategies.plain: Own Bitcoin while the MACD line is above its signal line.
rules: MACD = 12-day EMA minus 26-day EMA of closes; signal = 9-day EMA of MACD.
Long when MACD is above the signal line, cash when below.
strategies.interpretation: Default settings, no zero-line or trend filter.

strategies.name: Supertrend (10, 3)
strategies.plain: Own Bitcoin while the popular TradingView Supertrend line is green (price above an ATR-based trailing band).
rules: ATR period 10 (Wilder smoothing), multiplier 3, bands built from (high + low) ÷ 2 as in TradingView's formula.
Long while the trend is up, cash while it is down.

strategies.name: Bull Market Support Band
strategies.plain: The crypto-Twitter favorite: own Bitcoin while the weekly close is above both the 20-week SMA and the 21-week EMA.

sources.label: TradingView script: Bull Market Support Band (20w SMA, 21w EMA)

rules: Weekly bars close Sunday (UTC).
Buy when the weekly close is above both the 20-week SMA and 21-week EMA.
Sell when the weekly close is below both. Inside the band: keep the current state.
Fill on Monday's open.
strategies.interpretation: The script is an indicator, not a trading system; the buy-above / sell-below-both rule is our interpretation of how it is described.
